title: A Visit to the Clinic
author: Barashada Ingiriisiga
description: When Omar's daughter Hibo wakes with a hot forehead and a worried cry, he must take her to the clinic, learn to explain her symptoms in English, and trust the doctor's simple advice to help her heal.

chapters.title: A Hot Forehead
chapters.text:
Omar looked at his daughter, Hibo. She was sitting on the floor with her toys, but she was not playing. Her head was down and her eyes were half closed. "Hibo, are you okay?" Omar asked. She did not answer. He walked to her and put his hand on her forehead. It was very warm. Too warm.

"Hibo, you are very hot," Omar said. He felt scared. His little girl was usually full of energy. She ran and laughed all day. But today, she was quiet and tired. Her face was red and her eyes looked sad.

Omar picked her up. She felt heavy and soft in his arms. Her head rested on his shoulder. "I am tired, Baba," she said in a small voice. Omar's heart beat fast. He did not like to see his daughter sick.

He carried her to the sofa and put a soft blanket over her. Then he found his phone. His hands were a little shaky. He called the clinic. A woman answered. "Hello, my daughter has a fever," Omar said. "Her head is very hot and she is very tired." The woman's voice was calm. "Bring her to the clinic now," she said. "We will see her soon."

Omar put down the phone. He went to the bedroom and took a small bag. He put in a bottle of water, a light jacket for Hibo, and her favorite small toy, a brown bear. Then he went back to Hibo. "We are going to the clinic," he said softly. "The doctor will help you feel better."

Hibo opened her eyes. "I do not want to go," she said. Her voice was weak. Omar sat next to her and took her hand. "I know you are tired," he said gently. "But we will go together. It will be quick. And after, you can sleep in your bed."

He helped her stand up. She walked slowly, and Omar held her hand. At the door, he picked her up again. She was not heavy, but she felt very warm. He spoke to her in a quiet, soft voice. "You are a brave girl, Hibo. We will be at the clinic soon."

They walked to the bus stop. The sun was bright, but Omar did not feel warm. He only thought about Hibo. He looked at her face. Her eyes were closed. He held her close and waited for the bus.

questions.explanation: The text says Omar feels her forehead and it is very warm, and he says 'you are very hot' and calls the clinic about her fever.

questions.explanation: The text says 'He felt scared.' Also 'His heart beat fast.'

chapters.title: At the Clinic
chapters.text:
The clinic was a quiet place. The walls were white, and the lights were bright. Omar held Hibo's hand as they walked to the front desk. A kind nurse with a warm smile looked at them.

"Good morning," she said. "What is the problem today?"

Omar took a deep breath. "My daughter, Hibo, is not well. She has a fever."

The nurse nodded. "I see. Please come with me."

She led them to a small room. There was a bed, a chair, and a table with many things on it. Hibo sat on the bed. She looked very tired. Her eyes were heavy, and her face was red and warm.

"Can you tell me more about her symptoms?" the nurse asked.

Omar thought carefully. "Last night, she was very warm. I touched her head, and it was hot. She did not want to eat dinner. She said her body hurt."

The nurse wrote some notes. "Does she have a cough?"

"Yes," Omar said. "She coughs sometimes. Not all the time, but when she coughs, it sounds bad."

The nurse looked at Hibo. "And what about your throat, little one? Does it hurt?"

Hibo spoke in a small voice. "Yes. It hurts when I drink water."

The nurse smiled gently. "Thank you for telling me. I will check your temperature now."

She took a small machine and put it near Hibo's ear. It made a soft sound. Then she looked at the number on the machine.

"Her temperature is 38.5," the nurse said. "That is a fever, but not a very high one. That is good news."

Omar felt a little better. "So it is not too bad?"

"No, it is not too bad," the nurse said. "But we must help her feel better. Does she have a headache?"

"Yes," Hibo said. "My head hurts a little."

The nurse asked more questions. "Has she been sick before this week? Has she eaten anything different?"

Omar thought about it. "No, she has not been sick. We ate the same food as always. She plays outside with her friends, but she did not play yesterday. She was too tired."

The nurse wrote more notes. Then she put her hand on Hibo's shoulder. "You are doing very well. I will tell the doctor about you. He will come and see you soon."

She turned to Omar. "You did the right thing by bringing her here. Please wait. The doctor will be with you in a few minutes."

Omar smiled. "Thank you. I was worried."

The nurse smiled back. "That is normal. Parents always worry about their children. But you are here now, and we will help."

She left the room. Omar sat next to Hibo and held her hand. "You are brave," he said. "The doctor will help you feel better soon."

Hibo closed her eyes. Omar watched her and felt a little calmer. They were in the right place.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Advice
chapters.text:
The doctor came into the room. He had a kind face and a white coat. He looked at Hibo carefully. He put his hand on her head. Then he used a small light to look in her mouth. He listened to her chest with a stethoscope. Hibo was quiet and a little scared. Omar held her hand and smiled at her.

After the check, the doctor sat down. He looked at Omar and said, "Hibo has a viral fever. This is very common for children. It is not dangerous, but it makes her body hot and tired. The fever will go away, but we must help her."

Omar listened and nodded. He wanted to remember everything. The doctor gave him some good advice. First, Hibo must drink a lot of water and juice. The water helps her body fight the fever. Second, she must rest in bed. She should not play or run. Her body needs energy to get better. Third, the doctor gave Omar some medicine. He said, "Give her this medicine three times a day. Put a small spoon of the medicine in water and let her drink it. It will help reduce the fever and the pain in her throat."

The doctor also said, "Watch her for two days. If the fever stays high after two days, come back to the clinic. But I think she will get better soon."

Omar thanked the doctor. He put the medicine in his bag. Then he took Hibo's hand and said, "Let's go home, my dear." Hibo was very tired, but she smiled a little.

At home, Omar made a soft bed for Hibo on the sofa. He gave her a cup of warm water and then some juice. She drank slowly. He put a cool cloth on her forehead to help her feel better. She closed her eyes and slept for a long time.

In the evening, Omar gave Hibo the first dose of medicine. She did not like the taste. Her face showed that she wanted to refuse. But Omar said gently, "This will help you get better." Hibo drank it and made a funny face. They both laughed.

That night, Omar woke up to check on Hibo. He put his hand on her head. It was still warm, but not as warm as before. He was happy.

The next morning, Hibo woke up. She looked at her father and said, "I am hungry." Omar smiled. "That is a good sign," he said. He made her some warm soup. She ate a little and then slept again.

By the evening, Hibo's fever was almost gone. She sat up and started drawing pictures. Omar watched her and felt relieved. His worry was leaving his heart. He was proud of himself for taking care of his daughter. He was proud of Hibo too, because she was brave.

The doctor's advice was good. Omar followed it, and now his daughter was getting better. He knew that soon Hibo would be happy and strong again, and they would go to the park together.

questions.question: What did the doctor use to look in Hibo's mouth?
questions.explanation: The doctor used a small light to look in her mouth: 'Then he used a small light to look in her mouth.'

questions.question: What does the word 'fever' mean in this chapter?
options: A high body temperature caused by illness
questions.explanation: The doctor says Hibo has a viral fever that makes her body hot; fever refers to an abnormally high body temperature.

questions.question: According to the doctor, how many times a day should Hibo take the medicine?
questions.explanation: The doctor said, 'Give her this medicine three times a day.' So the correct answer is three times.

questions.question: Why did Omar put a cool cloth on Hibo's forehead?
options: To help her feel better from the fever
questions.explanation: The text says, 'He put a cool cloth on her forehead to help her feel better.' This help was for her fever.
